question.worked_solution:
Attempting to evaluate the limit by direct substitution leads to the indeterminate form $\frac{0}{0},$ as follows: 

$$
{lim}_{(x,y)\to (-1,1)}\frac{2{x}^{2}+3xy+{y}^{2}}{{x}^{3}+xy+{x}^{2}y+{y}^{2}}=\frac{2\cdot (-1)^{2}+3\cdot (-1)\cdot 1+{1}^{2}}{(-1)^{3}+(-1)\cdot 1+(-1)^{2}\cdot 1+{1}^{2}}=\frac{0}{0}
$$

However, we can simplify the limit by factoring the numerator and denominator and then canceling common factors:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{(x,y)\to (-1,1)}\frac{2{x}^{2}+3xy+{y}^{2}}{{x}^{3}+xy+{x}^{2}y+{y}^{2}} & ={lim}_{(x,y)\to (-1,1)}\frac{2{x}^{2}+2xy+xy+{y}^{2}}{{x}^{2}(x+y)+y(x+y)} \\  & ={lim}_{(x,y)\to (-1,1)}\frac{2x(x+y)+y(x+y)}{({x}^{2}+y)(x+y)} \\  & ={lim}_{(x,y)\to (-1,1)}\frac{(2x+y)(x+y)}{({x}^{2}+y)(x+y)} \\  & ={lim}_{(x,y)\to (-1,1)}\frac{2x+y}{{x}^{2}+y}\end{aligned}
$$

Now that the limit has been simplified, we can evaluate it:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{(x,y)\to (-1,1)}\frac{2x+y}{{x}^{2}+y} & =\frac{2(-1)+(1)}{(-1)^{2}+1} \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the limit evaluates to $-\frac{1}{2}.$
